description:
Bashie E Ring Bounce, v2 FULL MOTION. The owner approved the actual-character keys and their timed blocking: "this looks really good". Make ONE full take that connects these exact poses. The eight approved keys are in keys/result.json. Load them as the source of every semantic key; preserve their transforms exactly. This is motion authoring after key acceptance, not another keys-only job or a redesign.

The move has FOUR distinct parts: throw the ring clearly ahead while still down; small forward hop to it; a definite contact and compression; then a MUCH bigger upward bounce. Its readable two-jump structure is the primary goal. Do not smooth the whole thing into a single uninterrupted upward move. The body shapes and clock were accepted together.

Clock (60 Hz, 55 samples, 0.9 seconds):
0 ready, both hands carrying the ring at waist height.
12 throw/release, feet still down, open hands forward.
18 small-hop takeoff, ring already waiting ahead; arms open/back for balance.
26 small-hop apex, knees tucked, modest forward lean, down/forward intent.
34 both sandals connect to the near padded rim, a distinct first landing.
40 loaded crouch; hips lower about 0.08 m and the independent ring squashes.
44 big spring; long upward silhouette with arms raised/out beside hat.
54 high-rise handoff to air control.

This is a body-only clip. Do NOT animate the actor root or put the actual hop's vertical/forward arc into Hips. Only the already accepted local hips/torso compression and weight shifts belong here. Preview staging handles a small automatic root hop, 0.72 m forward: tick18 offset0, tick26 about0.54m up/0.36m ahead, tick34 at0.18m up/0.72m ahead. Ring top waits about0.18m above entry sole plane, ring center about0.97m ahead. It leaves the hands around8, travels forward on a small throw arc to16, then WAITS independently until feet connect at34. From34..40 the feet stay planted while the ring compresses. High actor ascent begins at44 at15m/s, separate from body animation. Preserve this staged action; no recovery-height change here.

Concentrate on natural mechanics within that clock. Throw: short anticipation, shoulders/chest and hands follow through, feet remain on the ordinary sole plane until the small hop. Keep contact with the carried ring plausible through8; its geometric center comes from both hands. Before18, heels may load without inventing an early leap. Small hop: modest push and compact legs, feet clear the rim, preserve the accepted tuck at26; on the way down open the legs into34 without abrupt knee/ankle flips. The first landing must visibly absorb into the crouch at40, then the high spring at44 has a sharp upward release, with arm/head follow-through into54. Preserve body/ring contact: keep both sandals near their approved sole plane and stance over34..40; solve planted feet as hips lower, rather than letting interpolation slide them. Do not let a uniform ease-to-each-key turn the throw/hop into a succession of freezes. Use a few breakdowns and deliberate per-channel spacing; protected semantic ticks still stay exact. No full-body overlap that moves those keys.

Actual short-limbed turtle rig is authoritative: 49 joints, rigid hat/head and shell, four cartoon fingers per hand, short arms and legs, sandals. Keep anatomy, proportions and all non-hips translations/scales unchanged. Forearms/hands must stay clear of torso, whistle, shell and hat; inspect the tucked apex and big raised-arm release on the actual mesh. Fingers remain plausible, no new fist or hand design. Keep actual knee/elbow bend direction and no elbow roll flips. The previous blocking's flow warnings are a reason to improve transitions, not to change protected poses.

Save result.json early, check fast while solving and full before finishing, inspect semantic sheets and complete timed playback. Do not buy additional references or start an unattended creative revision. Show the one resulting take to the owner before integration.
